functions.name: GetContextIdForWorld
functions.docs: Identifies a specific WorldContext that has objects which are allowed to tick and run tasks

functions.name: FActiveSyncWorkHandle
functions.docs: Used to specify how many times work should be executed as part of a sync point

functions.name: IsValid
functions.docs: True if this valid and has a name

functions.name: GetDependencyTickFunction
functions.docs:
Returns a raw pointer to the tick function that implements this handle which can be passed into AddPrerequisite.
This is only valid to call on the game thread and should not be cached.

functions.name: HasReservedWork
functions.docs: True if this handle has been used to reserve work. This will still be true until work is abandoned

functions.name: HasRequestedWork
functions.docs: True if this handle has been used to request work. This will still be true until work is abandoned

functions.name: ReserveFutureWork
functions.docs:
Request to reserve work using this handle, which must be filled to complete the frame's tasks.
If EveryFrame is passed in, it will reserve work at the start of every frame that must be requested or abandoned.

functions.name: RequestWork
functions.docs:
Requests that a tick function be executed by the sync point, this fills any reservations and may trigger tasks.
If EveryFrame is passed in, it will request the same function every frame until it is abandoned.

functions.name: AbandonWork
functions.docs:
Abandon any requested or reserved work and return to how it was at initial registration.
This clears HasReserved/HasRequested, but does not invalidate the handle.
Return true if there was any requested/reserved work to abandon.

functions.name: Reset
functions.docs: Completely reset this handle, which will abandon work and prevent any future use. This returns true if it was valid before

functions.name: FActiveSyncPoint
functions.docs: Struct defining an active sync point inside a specific world context, implemented as a tick function that may not be registered

functions.name: RegisterWorkHandle
functions.docs: Registers a new work handle that can be used to reserve and request work

functions.name: ReserveFutureWork
functions.docs: Uses handle to reserve work for later, that can be requested when ready

functions.name: RequestWork
functions.docs: Creates a new item of work bound to a specific function

functions.name: AbandonWork
functions.docs: Abandons requested or reserved work, which could trigger other work to start

functions.name: ResetWorkHandle
functions.docs: Resets a handle

functions.name: FTaskSyncManager
functions.docs: Registered sync point that created this

functions.name: Get
functions.docs: Return the global singleton if it exists

functions.name: FindDefaultBatch
functions.docs: Gets the default batch for a world context. This will return an invalid id if the world context is not set up for ticking

functions.name: FindSyncPoint
functions.docs:
Initializes a sync point id that can be passed between threads and used in the functions below.
This will return an invalid id if the name is not currently registered.
This function does not check that the sync point is enabled for the specific batch, that is handled in the other functions below.

functions.name: FindSyncPoint
functions.docs: Same as above, but using the default batch for the world context

functions.name: GetTaskGraphEvent
functions.signature: GetTaskGraphEvent(Target, Sync Point, Out Event Ref)
functions.docs:
Attempts to return the current frame's task graph event for this sync point, to pass as a dependency to other tasks.
This will fail if the task has not yet been created this frame or it has finished executing.

functions.name: TriggerSyncPoint
functions.docs: Manually triggers a sync point, this can only be called once per frame

functions.name: TriggerSyncPointAfterEvent
functions.signature: TriggerSyncPointAfterEvent(Target, Sync Point, Event To Wair For)
functions.docs: Tells the sync point to trigger at the completion of the passed in event/task, this is only possible if it hasn't already been triggered

functions.name: RegisterWorkHandle
functions.signature: RegisterWorkHandle(Target, Sync Point, Out Work Handle)
functions.docs:
Tries to creates a new sync work handle that can be used to reserve or request work to happen as part of a sync point.
If it was successful, OutWorkHandle will be set to a handle you can pass between threads and later fulfill or abandon.

functions.name: RegisterTickGroupWorkHandle
functions.signature: RegisterTickGroupWorkHandle(Target, World Context, Tick Group, Out Work Handle)
functions.docs:
Tries to creates a new sync work handle that can be used to reserve or request work to happen on the game thread during a tick group.
If it was successful, OutWorkHandle will be set to a handle you can use to request work for this frame or every frame (but not reserve).

functions.name: ReloadRegisteredData
functions.docs: Refresh the registered data from settings

functions.name: GetSyncPointDescription
functions.docs: Searches for a registered sync point, if ones is foundw ith that name it will return true and fill in OutDescription

functions.name: RegisterNewSyncPoint
functions.docs: Registers a new sync point at runtime. RegisteredName and SourceName must be filled out

functions.name: UnregisterSyncPoint
functions.docs: Unregisters a sync point, this will only delete if if both the registered and source names match

functions.name: CreateNewBatch
functions.docs: Allocates a new batch for the specified world, this will duplicate the events

functions.name: GetCurrentWorldContext
functions.docs: Gets the correct task world context for the current thread context. This will return an invalid context if called on worker threads

functions.name: GetTickFunctionForSyncPoint
functions.docs: Returns the tick function representing the specified event, if this returns a valid pointer you can use it for setting dependencies but it should not be modified or stored

functions.name: StartFrame
functions.signature: StartFrame(Target, In World, In Delta Seconds, In Tick Type)
functions.docs: Tells the manager that it is the start of a frame, which will register the appropriate events

functions.name: StartTickGroup
functions.signature: StartTickGroup(Target, In World, Tick Group, Ticks To Manual Dispatch)
functions.docs: Tells the manager that a tick group is starting for a specific world

functions.name: EndTickGroup
functions.docs: Tells the manager that a tick group is complete for a specific world, which could trigger events

functions.name: EndFrame
functions.docs: Tells the manager that it is the end of a frame and it will not start/end any more tick groups

functions.name: ReleaseWorldContext
functions.docs: Tells the manager that it should destroy all tracking info for a world context. This only needs to be called when destroying a test or preview world
